texts: good. the moon's new state, the day-and-year date and the past tense all come through with nothing dropped; the one wrinkle is on our side rather than yours -- our day term was written for month-days, so 'day 525' sits outside the range it was specified for.
good. 'a Keeper' is carried as an ordinary role type on Mira, wrapped in past tense, with no invented name atom.

bad: 'at the new-moon spring tide' is reduced to a bare spring-tide anchor, so the new-moon restriction is silently dropped and the time now fits any spring tide; the parse also dates the leading to day 525 by carrying sentence 1's frame over, which this sentence never states. Give the tide its own finite clause and hang the leading off it: 'The spring tide rose on day 525 of Year 2. During that tide Mira led a harvest party of three people to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.' Sentence 1 already records day 525 as the new moon, so the new-moon coincidence survives the rewrite.

mixed: the harvest, Mira and the salt-bloom land, but 'at the new moon' is dropped outright, and the only timing left is a day-and-year frame copied from sentence 1 that this sentence never states. State the day instead: 'On day 525 of Year 2, Mira harvested salt-bloom.' -- sentence 1 already records that day as the new moon, so the timing is not lost.

bad: 'nine buckets of salt-bloom' is stored as a measure whose dimension slot is filled with a marker reserved for a different construction, and no dimension word appears anywhere in the clause, so the count sits in a slot nothing will match; our instruction set also has no settled shape yet for container quantities. Make the buckets a counted set, and date the clause so the 'next morning' of sentence 6 has a day to count from: 'On day 525 of Year 2, the harvest party harvested salt-bloom and filled nine buckets with it.'

mixed: the report, Mira, the Council and the ordering after the harvest all land, but 'the next morning' yields only a bare morning with no day, because the harvest it follows carries no date. Date sentence 5 as suggested there, or put the day in this sentence: 'The next morning, on day 526 of Year 2, Mira reported the harvest to the Council.' With two harvests in the passage, note that the parse reads 'the harvest' as the party's nine-bucket one.
good. one congratulating event with the Council acting as a single body and Mira as the unchanged object -- nothing is wrongly distributed to individual councillors.
good. the recording points back at the same harvest the report did, with the Council as actor and no change asserted to the harvest itself.
